questions.q_en: Three taps P, Q and R alone can empty a tank in 8 hours, 4 hours, and 2 hours, respectively. When the tank is full, all three taps P, Q and R are opened one by one in the same order, but after an equal interval of 0.5 hour. In approximately how much time will the tank be empty?
questions.solution_en:
Part emptied by tap P in 1 hour = 1/8

Part emptied by tap Q in 1 hour = 1/4

Part emptied by tap R in 1 hour = 1/2

Let the time in which the tank is emptied be 'x' hours

Tap P was open for = x hours

Tap Q was open for = (x - 0.5) hours

Tap R was open for = (x - 1) hours

Now, part emptied by tank in x hours = 1

=> x/8 + (x - 0.5)/4 + (x - 1)/2 = 1

=> x/8 + (2x - 1)/8 + (4x - 4)/8 = 1

=> x + 2x - 1 + 4x - 4 = 8

=> 7x = 13

=> x = 13/7 hours ≅ 1 hour 51 min.

So, the tank will be empty in approximately 1 hour 51 min

questions.q_en: Inlet pipes, R and S can fill a tank in 50 minutes and 72 minutes respectively. Outlet pipes D and E together can empty the tank in 60 minutes. When pipes D and R are opened together, then the tank is filled in 96 minutes. In how many minutes (approximately) will the tank be filled if the pipes S and E are opened together?
questions.solution_en:
Let the total work be 7200 units (LCM of 50, 72, 60 and 96)

Work done by R in a day = 7200/50 = 144 units

Work done by S in a day = 7200/72 = 100 units

Work done by E and D in a day = 7200/60 = 120 units

Work done by R and D in a day = 7200/96 = 75 units

So, work done by D in a day = 144 - 75 = 69 units

So, work done by E in a day = 120 - 69 = 51 units

When S and E are opened together, work done = 100 - 51= 49 units

So, total time taken to fill the tank = 7200/49 = 146.93 ~ 147 minutes

questions.q_en: Pipe A can fill a tank in 72 minutes and pipe B can fill the same tank at 15 m3/minute. If the volume of the tank is 540 m3, then find the time taken by pipe A and pipe B together to fill the tank together.
questions.solution_en:
Volume of the tank = 540 m3

Time taken by pipe B = 540/15 = 36 minutes

Total capacity (LCM of 36 and 72) = 72 units

Efficiency of pipe A = 72/72 = 1 units/minute

Efficiency of pipe B = 72/36 = 2 units/minute

Time taken by pipe A and B together to fill the tank = 72/(1 + 2) = 24 minutes

questions.q_en: Pipe A and B can fill a tank in 8 minutes and 12 minutes respectively. Both the pipes are opened. The tank got filled in 6 minutes if pipe A is turned off after -
questions.solution_en:
Capacity of tank = LCM of 8 and 12 = 24 unit

Efficiency of pipe A = 24/8 = 3 units/minute

Efficiency of pipe B = 24/12 = 2 units/minute

Let pipe A turned off after 'x' minutes

According to question,

(3 + 2)x + 2(6 - x) = 24

5x + 12 - 2x = 24

3x = 12

x = 4 minutes

questions.q_en: Pipe P and Q can fill a tank in 3 minutes and 12 minutes respectively and pipe R can empty it in 15 minutes. Find the time taken to fill the tank when all pipes are opened together.
questions.solution_en:
Capacity of tank = LCM of 3, 12 and 15 = 60 unit

Efficiency of pipe P = 60/3 = 20 units/minute

Efficiency of pipe Q = 60/12 = 5 units/minute

Efficiency of pipe R = 60/15 = 4 units/minute

Required time = 60/(20 + 5 - 4) = 60/21 or 20/7 = 2(6/7) minutes

questions.q_en: Two pipes P and Q fill a tank in 140 minutes and 52.5 minutes respectively. A third pipe R can empty it at __ liters/minute. When all three pipes are opened together, then the tank is filled in 1 hour. If the capacity of the tank is 630 liters, then what should come in place of the given blank?
questions.solution_en:
P = 140 minutes, Q = 52.5 minutes

When all pipes are opened together, then the tank is filled in 1 hour (or 60 minutes). This means filling rate is more than the emptying rate. So,

1/60 = 1/P + 1/Q - 1/R

1/60 = 1/140 + 1/52.5 - 1/R

R = 105 minutes

Let R can empty the tank it at X liters/minute.

Since, the capacity of the tank is 630 liters, then

X = 630/105

X = 6

questions.q_en: If 17/25 part of a tank is filled by a pipe in 14 minutes 10 seconds, then rest part of the tank will be filled in -
questions.solution_en:
14 minutes 10 seconds = (14 * 60 + 10) seconds = 850 seconds

Total part of the tank will be filled in = 850 * 25/17 = 1250 seconds

Therefore, remaining part of the tank will be filled in = 1250 - 850 = 400 seconds = 6 minutes 40 seconds

questions.q_en: A pipe can fill a tank in 20 minutes and another pipe can fill a tank in 30 minutes. Pipe A is opened for half of the time and pipe A and B are opened for the other half. How long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution_en:
"

In 1 min pipe A can fill 1/20 of the tank

In 1 min pipe B can fill 1/30 of the tank

In 1 min pipe A and B together can fill 1/20+1/30=1/12 of the tank

Say pipe A only opened for x mins and pipes A and B together opened for x mins

Then portion of tank filled

= x/20+x/12 = 1

or (3x+5x)/60=1

or 8x/60=1

or 2x=15

So time taken to fill the tank = 2x=15 minutes

"

questions.q_en: Two inlet pipes P and Q and one outlet pipe R are attached to a tank. Pipes P and Q can individually fill the tank in 90 minutes and 180 minutes respectively. If pipes P, Q, and R are opened simultaneously, the tank is full in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much time will be taken by pipe R to empty the full tank?
questions.solution_en:
Pipes P and Q can individually fill the tank in 90 minutes and 180 minutes respectively.

If pipes P, Q, and R are opened simultaneously, the tank is full in 1 hour 40 minutes.

Pipe R alone can empty the tank in = 1/(1/100 - 1/90 - 1/180) = -150

Hence, R alone can empty the tank in = 150 minutes

questions.q_en: Pipe A and pipe B together can fill a cistern in 28 minutes, pipe B and pipe C together can fill the same cistern in 42 minutes, and pipe A and pipe C together can fill the same cistern in 56 minutes. Find the time taken by pipe C alone to fill the cistern.
questions.solution_en:
The capacity of a cistern = L.C.M of 28, 42, and 56 = 168

Efficiency = total capacity/ time taken

Efficiency of pipe A and pipe B = 168/28 = 6

Efficiency of pipe B and pipe C = 168/42 = 4

Efficiency of pipe A and pipe C = 168/56 = 3

Efficiency of pipe A, pipe B, and pipe C = (6 + 4 + 3)/2 = 13/2

Efficiency of pipe C = 13/2 - 6 = 1/2

The required value = 168/ (1/2) = 336 minutes = 5 hours 36 minutes

questions.q_en: Pipe A functions at a uniform rate. It is found that at 11: 00 am, 5/11th of tank is filled by pipe A and by 12: 31 pm, 3/4th of the tank is filled by the pipe A. How long does it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution_en:
At 11: 00 am, 5/11th of tank is filled and by 12: 31 pm, 3/4th of tank is filled.

In 91 min, part of tank is filled = (3/4) - (5/11) = (33 - 20)/44 = 13/44th

Full tank is filled in = 91 * 44/13 = 308 min.

questions.q_en: A pipe can fill a tank in 28 hours. Due to a leakage in the bottom, it is filled in 32 hours. If the tank is 50% full, how much time will the leak take to empty the tank?
questions.solution_en:
Let total capacity of tank = LCM of 28 and 32 = 224 units

Efficiency of pipe = 224/28 = 8 units per hour

Efficiency of leak and pipe = 224/32 = 7 units per hour

Net efficiency of leak = 7 - 8 = -1 units per hour [- shows leak will empty the tank]

50% of total capacity = 224 * ½ = 112 units

Required time = 112/1 = 112 hours.

questions.q_en: Pipe P can fill a tank in 20 days. If pipe P is 20% more efficient than pipe Q, then in what time can P and Q together complete the whole work?

Ratio of efficiency of P and Q = 120:100 = 6:5

Efficiency of P and Q together = 6 + 5 = 11 units

Time taken by P and Q together = (6 * 20)/11 = 120/11 = 10(10/11) days

Time taken by both pipes together to fill the tank = 120/(5 - 3) = 60 minutes

questions.q_en: Pipe P, pipe Q and pipe R can fill a tank in 18 minutes, 54 minutes and 72 minutes respectively. Pipe P and pipe Q both are opened for 9 minutes. Find the time taken by pipe R alone to fill the remaining tank.
questions.solution_en:
Capacity of tank = LCM of 18, 54 and 72 = 216 unit

Efficiency of pipe P = 216/18 = 12 unit

Efficiency of pipe Q = 216/54 = 4 unit

Efficiency of pipe R = 216/72 = 3 unit

Part of tank got filled in 9 minutes = 9 * (12 + 4) = 144 unit

Remaining part = 216 - 144 = 72 unit

Time taken by pipe R alone to fill the remaining tank = 72/3 = 24 minutes
